title: Feature
description: A unit of product functionality that a persona can directly perceive and invoke, such as a screen, command, setting or behaviour. It is described in user terms and can be prioritised, sized and scheduled on its own, and it realises one or more product capabilities. Use Capability instead when the element names an ability the product must have regardless of which user-visible functionality provides it, and is not itself prioritised or sized as a deliverable. Use UserWorkflow instead when the element is a goal-directed sequence of user actions that passes through one or more features rather than a single piece of functionality. Use WorkflowStep instead when the element is one ordered action or experience within a specific user journey that exercises a feature, rather than the functionality itself. Use Milestone instead when the element is a dated delivery target that groups features, rather than functionality the user interacts with.
x-dr-standard: Product Management Practice: Feature (backlog/roadmap item). There is no direct ArchiMate 3.2 element; it is modelled as realising a Strategy Capability (§7.3.1).
x-dr-evidence: a feature-flag definition (e.g. LaunchDarkly, Unleash or a features.yml key) that gates a user-visible behaviour such as 'bulk-export' or 'dark-mode'
a Gherkin .feature file whose 'Feature:' block describes user-facing functionality with acceptance scenarios
a release-notes, changelog or user-guide entry announcing user-visible functionality (e.g. 'New: export reports to CSV') that is traceable to a set of routes, views or endpoints
